puzzles.description: Prove your deeper Kiro knowledge. Before each question pick a confidence stake — higher stakes show fewer choices but score more. Hit the target to restore the codebase.

questions.question: How do you connect Kiro to external tools and data sources?
options: MCP — the Model Context Protocol for external tool servers
A curated plugins marketplace built into the IDE
Language-specific SDK adapters you install per project
Direct REST calls hard-coded into each steering file
questions.answer: MCP — the Model Context Protocol for external tool servers

questions.question: What happens when Kiro's conversation approaches the context limit?
options: Compaction summarizes older history so the session continues
The oldest messages are silently dropped from the thread
It automatically switches to a smaller, cheaper model
The session ends and must be restarted from scratch
questions.answer: Compaction summarizes older history so the session continues

questions.question: Where does Kiro's shared project configuration live?
options: In the .kiro/ directory committed to the repository
In a per-user cloud dashboard tied to your account
Inside package.json under a 'kiro' config key
In the .vscode/ workspace settings folder
questions.answer: In the .kiro/ directory committed to the repository

questions.question: Which surfaces run Kiro's single unified agent?
options: IDE, CLI, Web, and Mobile — all backed by one harness
The desktop IDE and a companion browser extension only
A cloud web console with a read-only mobile viewer
The CLI for CI plus a separate IDE-only agent
questions.answer: IDE, CLI, Web, and Mobile — all backed by one harness

questions.question: How is a Kiro Power different from a plain MCP server?
options: A Power bundles an MCP server with knowledge, loaded on demand
A Power is a paid, higher-throughput tier of an MCP server
A Power is an MCP server that runs on managed GPU hardware
A Power is a renamed MCP server with no functional change
questions.answer: A Power bundles an MCP server with knowledge, loaded on demand

questions.question: In Kiro's permission system, how are conflicting rules resolved?
options: Deny overrides ask, and ask overrides allow
Allow always wins so the agent is never blocked
The most recently added rule takes precedence
The user is prompted to resolve every conflict manually
questions.answer: Deny overrides ask, and ask overrides allow

questions.question: What does Kiro's Checkpoints and rewind feature let you do?
options: Undo agent changes or fork a conversation at an earlier turn
Save named snapshots of the IDE layout and settings
Roll back a deployed release to a previous version
Auto-commit the working tree every few minutes
questions.answer: Undo agent changes or fork a conversation at an earlier turn

puzzles.description: Prove you understand WHY AI-DLC works. Pick a confidence stake before each question — higher stakes score more but show fewer choices. Hit the target to validate the design.

questions.question: What does 'Reimagine, don't retrofit' mean for AI-DLC?
options: Design a new AI-native lifecycle rather than adding AI to Agile
Modernize the legacy codebase before adopting any AI tooling
Keep Scrum ceremonies but let AI run the daily standups
Automate the existing SDLC phases without changing the roles
questions.answer: Design a new AI-native lifecycle rather than adding AI to Agile

questions.question: Why does AI-DLC 'reverse the conversation' between human and AI?
options: AI proposes plans and asks clarifying questions; humans validate and decide
Humans author every requirement first and AI only fills in the code
AI runs end to end autonomously and reports results afterward
The product owner queues tasks that AI executes one by one
questions.answer: AI proposes plans and asks clarifying questions; humans validate and decide

questions.question: Why does AI-DLC shorten cycles to hours or days instead of weeks?
options: AI absorbs the manual heavy-lifting that forced long iteration cycles
Shorter cycles reduce cloud compute and licensing costs
It mirrors the two-week cadence teams already know from Scrum
Frequent restarts are needed because AI output is unreliable
questions.answer: AI absorbs the manual heavy-lifting that forced long iteration cycles

questions.question: What does AI-DLC change that 'AI-assisted coding' alone does not?
options: AI drives planning and design across the lifecycle, not just coding
It fine-tunes the model on your private repository automatically
It guarantees zero defects by generating exhaustive tests
It replaces the IDE with a fully cloud-based environment
questions.answer: AI drives planning and design across the lifecycle, not just coding

questions.question: Why does AI-DLC keep humans in the loop instead of full autonomy?
options: Humans own validation, risk, and the decisions AI shouldn't make alone
Current models cannot generate production code without help
Regulations require a human to sign off only at final release
It intentionally throttles AI so the team can keep pace
questions.answer: Humans own validation, risk, and the decisions AI shouldn't make alone

questions.question: In AI-DLC, what is the human's role during an AI-proposed plan?
options: Review, adjust, and approve at decision points before AI proceeds
Write the plan from scratch and hand it to the AI to execute
Stay hands-off until the AI has finished the whole task
Only estimate story points and assign the work
questions.answer: Review, adjust, and approve at decision points before AI proceeds

questions.question: How does AI-DLC treat design techniques like domain modeling?
options: They're woven into the AI-driven workflow, not left as an afterthought
They're skipped entirely to maximize raw coding speed
They're done once upfront and never revisited
They're outsourced to a separate architecture team
questions.answer: They're woven into the AI-driven workflow, not left as an afterthought

hints: 💬 Kiro: "Think about the WHY, not the what. AI-DLC is a whole new lifecycle, not Agile-plus-AI. AI leads planning; humans own the decisions."
💬 Kiro: "Reimagine = new AI-native lifecycle. Reverse conversation = AI drafts, humans validate. Rapid cycles = AI removed the manual heavy-lifting."
💬 Kiro: "Pick the answer that keeps humans owning decisions while AI drives execution."
